title: Maximum Number of Distinct Elements After Operations
summary: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, you can add an integer in the range [-k, k] to each element at most once.
statement: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, you can add an integer in the range [-k, k] to each element at most once. Return the highest count of unique elements possible in nums after these operations.
constraints: nums has up to 100,000 positive integers and k is nonnegative.
Each element may independently become any integer in its inclusive interval [value-k,value+k].
Maximize the number of distinct final values.
hints: Each number supplies an interval of possible final integer values.
Sort intervals by center and greedily take the smallest available integer after the previous assignment.
Choose min(right endpoint, max(left endpoint, previous+1)); count it when it advances.
Using the earliest feasible value leaves at least as much room for every later interval as any larger choice.
editorial: Using the earliest feasible value leaves at least as much room for every later interval as any larger choice.

tests.explanation: Assign the six intervals consecutive values from negative one through four, making all elements distinct.
The three copies can become four, five, and six, so all three are distinct.
